claims.statement: For every finite tree T, original leaf v with support s, and integer k, P_(T-v)(z)=P_H(z)+zP_R(z), hence Delta_k(T-v)=Delta_k(H)+Delta_(k-1)(R); at any integer p the favorable-original-leaf aggregate is the sum over distinct original leaf tags satisfying Delta_p(H_v)+Delta_(p-1)(R_v)<0 of Delta_(p-1)(H_v)-Delta_(p-1)(R_v).
claims.scope: Universal exact branch identity and selector/summand re-expression for finite ordinary trees, all integer k and p; no sign conclusion.
claims.reason: Direct partition of independent sets in T-v proves the coefficient and difference identities with the original closed neighborhood and correct index shift, including zero-extended edge ranks and shared-support leaf multiplicity. Copied-code replay agrees with the source but is not independent. Separate closed-form integer calculations for P60 and T60 verify alpha, first strict descent, selector values, summands and complete sums at p=alpha-2. Neither the identity nor these two examples proves the primary aggregate sign.

limitations: Numerical checks cover only P60 and T60 at p=alpha-2; they are not universal evidence.
The branch identity gives no global compensation argument for the selector-restricted aggregate, so the primary claim remains open.
No Lean build was run under the critique-stage protocol.
